band_placement.customer_value: merged pull requests the repository landed in a 14-day window, ANY AUTHOR. The cohort's axis is frame.py's count(DISTINCT pr) of merged PullRequestEvents with no author predicate, so excluding machine-authored merges here would place a bump-heavy repository one or more bands too low.
band_placement.derivation: The fitter places a repository that did not define the cut by RANK, not by interval: fit._place_unbanded does bands[bisect_left(keys, (value, repo))] over the support units' (panel_prs_per_period, repo) order. A customer is not in that order, and its repository name must not decide its cohort, so the customer's key is (value, '') — the empty string sorts below every repository name, which is bisect_left's own tie behaviour taken to its limit. bisect_left then returns the FIRST index whose value is >= the customer's, whose band b* therefore satisfies value <= high(b*); and every band below b* holds only values strictly below the customer's, so high(b) < value there. b* is exactly min{b : value <= high(b)}. The high edges are monotone non-decreasing because the cut is a rank cut over a sorted list, so the scan is well defined. Ranges OVERLAP at ties (coderabbit band 0 is 2..2 and band 1 is 2..3) which is why 'the band whose interval contains the value' is not a function and this rule reads one edge only.
band_placement.rule: band = the LOWEST index b whose published panel_prs_per_period HIGH edge is at least the customer's value; when the value exceeds every high edge, the LAST band. The LOW edges are never read.
band_placement.walk_budget_rule: min(150, round(panel_prs_per_period * 90 / 14)) — the per-repository pull-request population cap the walk enforced, reproduced exactly on all 2,204 corpus repo rows. The customer's population is the walk_budget most-recently-updated pull requests in the repository, filtered afterwards.

expected.note: one entry per (repository, vendor) unit, in the fold's own stable order. Compare counters FIRST: a metric value alone says something is wrong, a counter says which population and which gate. Every value is an IEEE-754 double produced by one division of the two integers in `counters`, so agreement is EXACT — compare with === and never with a tolerance.

acted_on_rate.definition: Share of settled, fully-read vendor threads that were resolved OR followed by a human after the vendor's last comment. Deliberately EXCLUDES is_outdated — see acted_on_rate_with_outdated for the other reading; the two are emitted side by side so the sensitivity is visible rather than argued about.
acted_on_rate.numerator: settled complete vendor threads: is_resolved OR human_followed_last_review_bot

acted_on_rate_with_outdated.definition: acted_on_rate widened by GitHub's is_outdated flag. A SEPARATE METRIC, never a redefinition of the one above: the two answer 'was this dealt with' under two different beliefs about whether a changed line proves it.
acted_on_rate_with_outdated.numerator: settled complete vendor threads: resolved OR outdated OR followed

cross_bot_overlap_rate.definition: Share of this vendor's anchored settled threads whose (path, line) anchor also carries a DIFFERENT vendor's thread on the same pull request — how often two bots say something about the same line. A thread that lost its line (outdated, no line) has no anchor and is excluded from both halves rather than counted as non-overlapping.
cross_bot_overlap_rate.denominator: settled vendor threads with a (path, line) anchor
cross_bot_overlap_rate.numerator: anchored vendor threads sharing (path, line) with another vendor on the same PR

findings_per_merged_pr.definition: Non-empty comment bodies this vendor left, per merged human-authored pull request. An empty-body review (a silent approval) is NOT a finding — 89 of 1,204 bot comment rows in the smoke walk were exactly that, and counting them would score a bot that approves without words above one that writes.

human_followed_last_bot_rate.definition: Share of settled, fully-read vendor threads where a human commented strictly after the vendor's LAST comment — engagement that survived the bot's final word rather than a reply that preceded it.
human_followed_last_bot_rate.numerator: settled complete vendor threads with human_followed_last_review_bot

human_reply_rate.definition: Share of this vendor's settled, fully-read review threads where a human commented after the vendor's first comment. ⚠ Threads whose comment tail was truncated are EXCLUDED: 'nobody answered' and 'we did not read far enough to know' are different claims, and the corpus nulls the fact rather than defaulting it to False.
human_reply_rate.numerator: settled complete vendor threads with human_replied

median_hours_to_first_human_reply.definition: Per-repository median of the time from this vendor's FIRST comment on a thread to the first human comment after it, over settled threads that got one. The clock starts at the first BOT comment rather than the thread root, because a thread a human opened and a bot joined has a root that is not a bot finding at all.
median_hours_to_first_human_reply.denominator: settled complete vendor threads that received a human reply

overdue_untouched_rate_168h.definition: Of this vendor's review threads that were at least 168h old at observation and whose comment tail was fully read, the share that are neither resolved nor answered by a human. Threads younger than the grace window are EXCLUDED from the denominator, not counted as answered: they have not had the chance to be overdue.
overdue_untouched_rate_168h.numerator: threads age>=168h, complete, not resolved, no human reply

overdue_untouched_rate_72h.definition: Of this vendor's review threads that were at least 72h old at observation and whose comment tail was fully read, the share that are neither resolved nor answered by a human. Threads younger than the grace window are EXCLUDED from the denominator, not counted as answered: they have not had the chance to be overdue.
overdue_untouched_rate_72h.numerator: threads age>=72h, complete, not resolved, no human reply

pr_comment_coverage.definition: Share of merged human-authored pull requests on which this vendor said anything. ⚠ CONDITIONED ON THE VENDOR BEING LIVE IN THIS POPULATION: a repo where it emitted nothing on any merged pull request is UNDEFINED here, not 0.0 — counted under vendor_silent when there is no trace of it in the repository at all, and under vendor_absent_from_population when it reviewed only pull requests that had not merged. The floor of this metric is therefore 1/N, and that is the honest reading — 'the bot is installed but never fires' is a different claim from 'the bot is not installed', and this corpus cannot tell them apart.
pr_comment_coverage.numerator: merged human-authored PRs with >= 1 vendor finding

thread_outdated_rate.definition: Share of this vendor's settled review threads GitHub marks outdated — the anchored lines changed after the comment. ⚠ THIS IS NOT 'likely addressed'. The host product's likely_addressed asks whether a commit touched the thread's FILE after its last comment, computed from commit file lists this walk does not fetch. The two are close enough to be confused and differ by percentage points, so they have different names and this corpus carries only the one it observed.

thread_resolved_rate.definition: Share of this vendor's settled review threads marked resolved on GitHub. isResolved is a thread-level scalar the walk observes even under comment truncation, so this metric's denominator is all settled threads rather than only complete ones.

threads_per_merged_pr.definition: Review threads carrying at least one comment from this vendor, per merged human-authored pull request. A thread two vendors both commented on counts for both — the question is what each vendor generated, not how the work was divided.
threads_per_merged_pr.numerator: review threads with this vendor in review_bot_vendors

populations.outcome: human-authored, detail-observed pull requests, MERGED OR NOT. Conditioning a thread outcome on the merge selects on the dependent variable; the censoring problem merging solves for volume is solved here by settle_hours instead.
populations.volume: merged, human-authored, detail-observed pull requests. Merged because an open pull request is still accumulating comments — its count is right-censored and averaging it in understates every vendor.

input.note: a NEUTRAL schema: it names no column of either side. Each field's mapping onto the corpus and onto the host's tables is in the contract document.

repos.purpose: the happy path: every metric fitted with a non-trivial, non-degenerate value. Ten merged human pull requests, two merged machine-authored ones (excluded from the volume denominator, counted in the machine disclosure), one open one.

RULE 4. The panel says coderabbit runs here; the walk read the repository and saw nothing from it. Every metric is vendor_silent — UNDEFINED, never 0.0. Uninstalled, path-scoped and category-suppressed are indistinguishable from here and all three differ from 'commented and was ignored'.

RULE 4's own failure mode, wearing a gate's clothes. The vendor is demonstrably live — busy on pull requests that had not merged — so the OUTCOME metrics are perfectly good, while the three VOLUME metrics are vendor_absent_from_population rather than a measured 0.0. Fitting this as a hard zero is what manufactures 'this bot finds nothing'.

DENOMINATOR_EMPTY, and why it is not a zero. A summariser posts PR-level comments and opens no review threads at all: its volume metrics fit, and every thread-outcome metric has an EMPTY population. 0.0 there would be a lie about its behaviour.

BELOW_MIN_UNITS, and the split between the two floors. Three settled complete threads: the ten metrics at min_units=5 refuse, and median_hours_to_first_human_reply (min_units=3) FITS on the same repository. A per-repository rate over two threads is noise wearing a percentage sign; a fixture with one floor would not notice the other.

repos.host_note: the host has no equivalent: a repository it cannot read has no rows at all, so this exclusion can never fire customer-side. It ships to pin the corpus-side guard ORDER — repo_not_walked is tested BEFORE vendor_silent, and a repository with partial rows under a failed walk must not be read as a quiet vendor.
repos.purpose: REPO_NOT_WALKED — a survivorship loss, not a silence and not a zero. The repository was deleted, renamed or made private between the frame window and the walk. It is a member of its cell and of nothing else.

EVERY MERGE IS MACHINE-AUTHORED, so the volume population is empty — and the exclusion is vendor_absent_from_population, NOT denominator_empty, because a vendor with no merged human pull request to comment on cannot have been observed in that population either. ⚠ A VOLUME denominator_empty IS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: a comment only enters the volume population from a pull request that is merged, human-authored and detail-observed, which is itself a member of merged_eligible. The TypeScript side must model it as unreachable rather than as an untested branch. Dependency bumps are 30-40% of merges in the wild and their review dynamics are nothing like human work.

THE REAL ZERO rule 4 exists to protect. The vendor is live on merged pull requests and said nothing worth counting — every one of its comments is an empty-body review. findings_per_merged_pr and pr_comment_coverage are a MEASURED 0.0 with full weight, structurally distinct from the undefined zeros above.

CROSS_BOT_OVERLAP_RATE and the anchor rule. Two vendors on the same (path, line) of the same pull request overlap; a thread that lost its line has NO anchor and is excluded from BOTH halves rather than counted as non-overlapping. A thread two vendors both commented on counts for both — the question is what each generated.

THE GRACE BOUNDARIES, both of them, and the fact that the overdue family does NOT chain through settle_hours. Threads at exactly 72h and exactly 168h ARE eligible (>=); one second under is not. A truncated thread is out of the overdue denominator entirely, because 'nobody answered' and 'we did not read far enough to know' are different claims and only the second is true of it.

THE MEDIAN'S TIE CONVENTION. Four reply times, so the median is the MEAN OF THE TWO MIDDLE VALUES and not the lower of them — the one place where a reimplementation silently disagrees on an even sample. The clock starts at the vendor's FIRST comment on the thread, never at the thread root.

repos.host_note: not constructible host-side: the host DERIVES a thread's vendor set from its comments' authors, so a thread cannot name a vendor that wrote nothing on it. It ships to pin the gate's identity on the corpus side.
repos.purpose: THE LIVE GATE IS comments_observed, NOT THE THREAD COUNTERS. This repository's threads name the vendor in review_bot_vendors while no comment row carries it, so every counter it feeds is non-zero and every metric is still vendor_silent. Reading the gate off the thread counters instead would fit a distribution nobody observed.

repos.host_note: the host syncs detail for every pull request it holds, so customer-side EVERY pull request in the population is detail-observed. The TypeScript reference implementation hard-codes that and says so; the case ships so the corpus-side gate stays pinned.
repos.purpose: A pull request the walk ENUMERATED and never READ. Its detail never landed, so its threads and comments are ABSENT rather than zero and it is out of BOTH populations — the survivorship claim repo_not_walked makes one level up, made per pull request.
